data.cultural_impact: The Yadu dynasty is a significant clan in Hindu mythology, mentioned several times in various Hindu scriptures including the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita. The Yadavas, as they are popularly known, were the descendants of King Yadu and are believed to be direct descendants of Lord Krishna. The name "Yaduvanshi" or "Yaduvanshiya" signifies one belonging to the Yadu clan. This name carries immense cultural significance for those who trace their lineage to this revered clan. It is a source of great pride and a powerful symbol of heritage and tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Yaduvanshi" contains spiritual significance as well. Lord Krishna, who was the deity of this clan, was an avatar of Vishnu, the preserver deity in Hinduism. The name serves as a reminder of the spiritual connection of the individual to the divine. It imbues the person with the virtues and values taught by Krishna and inspires them to live a righteous and virtuous life. The name is a constant source of inspiration and guidance, encouraging the individual to tread the spiritual path wherever they go in life.

historical_references.reference: The Yadavas or Yadu-Vanshi were a prominent dynasty of ancient India, tracing their lineage to the mythological character Yadu, a descendant of the god Krishna. They were known to have ruled significant territories in the northern and central parts of India during the Mahabharata War (around 3100 BCE).

The Yadavas continued to hold power in several parts of India through various dynasties like the Haihayas, the Valour-Kshatriyas, and the Jats, who claimed descent from the Yadavas. The last major Yadava ruler was Harshad Deva of the Haihayas, who ruled in the 11th century CE in the region of Bihar and Bengal.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'यदुवंशी' (Yadavamshi) translates to 'Descendant of the Yadava Dynasty' in Sanskrit. This name holds significant relevance in Indian history and mythology, as the Yadavas were believed to be the kinsmen of Lord Krishna. Today, this name is seen on various platforms, including Facebook groups, Reddit communities, and Wikipedia pages, where individuals and communities explore and discuss the rich history, mythology, and genealogy of the Yadavas.

name_in_real_life.story: Devi यदुवंशी from Delhi, India embodies the meaning of यदुवंशी - "Descendant of Yadu". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name "Yaduvanshi" signifies one who belongs to the Yadu dynasty, a revered lineage in Hindu mythology, traced back to Lord Krishna. It symbolizes a connection to the divine and the virtues of truth, righteousness, and unwavering devotion.
